apps.description: Lightweight browser with ADM, ad blocking, media capture, and multi-profile support
apps.releaseNotes:
# Clint Browser v1.2.0

---

## Announcement

Before I discuss the changelog, I have an announcement. This is important for the future of Clint Browser. I'm planning to switch Clint to use GeckoView.

For more details and to vote on the poll:

[ClintBrowser Discussion #67](https://github.com/jhaiian/ClintBrowser/discussions/67)

---

## What's New

### Profiles

Now you can stay signed in to **multiple accounts on the same website at the same time**. Each profile keeps its own cookies and site data, so they never mix with each other.

- **Default** — Your existing logins and site data. This is always there and can't be deleted.
- **Create your own profiles** — Give each one a name and pick a color from 8 colors. The next color is picked for you automatically.
- **Edit** — Rename a profile or change its color anytime.
- **Clear data** — Signs you out of every website in that profile and removes its cookies and site data, but keeps the profile.
- **Delete** — Permanently deletes the profile and all of its logins, cookies and site data.
  - If a tab is still using that profile, it will tell you to close those tabs first. If you're sure you already closed them, restart the app and try again.

**Where to find it**

- **Browser Settings → Profiles**
- Add **New tab in profile…** to your browser menu through Menu customization. Long-press it to jump straight to Profiles.
- It's also in the **Tab Menu** three-dot menu.
- Pick a profile in the picker dialog when you open a new tab, or tap **Manage** to open Profiles. If you don't have any profile yet, it takes you to Profiles to create one.

**How it behaves**

- Links and popups you open from a tab stay in the **same profile** as that tab.
- **Incognito never uses profiles.**
- Tabs in the Tab Grid show a small badge with the profile color and name.
- Your tabs remember their profile after you close and reopen the app.
- Downloads, saving images, and media/stream capture now use the cookies of the profile you're in. That means downloads from sites you're logged in to still work.
- **Backup & Restore** now includes your profiles and each profile's cookies.

> *Profiles need a newer version of Android System WebView. If your WebView is too old, Clint will show an "Update WebView" message and the menu item will be hidden. Update it in Google Play or wherever you get WebView from.*

(Thanks to u/Interesting-Stick641 on Reddit for suggesting this)

---

### Media Capture

- Subtitles from HLS streams are now detected, previewed, and downloaded. Clint reads the playlist, fetches the subtitle segments, and merges them into one subtitle file.
- Subtitle preview now shows the cue count and duration for HLS subtitle playlists too.
- **Convert TS to MP4 or AAC** — audio-only streams can now be converted to a standard AAC file instead of being left as raw TS.
- Added a minimum size for a normal video to be shown.

(Thanks to @reviewlord for reporting this #71)

---

### Shortcut Manager

A new page to view and manage every shortcut you've added to your home screen. It replaces the old global **Frameless** toggle in Browser Settings.

**Where to find it**

- **Browser Settings → Shortcut Manager**
- Long-press **Create a Shortcut** in the browser menu.

**What you can do**

- See all your shortcuts with their icon, name and when they were created.
- **Search** your shortcuts.
- **Sort** by Title or Date Created, ascending or descending.
- **Select multiple** shortcuts and delete them at once.
- Use the three-dot menu on each shortcut for **Settings**, **Create a Shortcut** and **Delete**.
  - **Create a Shortcut** puts it on your home screen again. If it's already there, it tells you instead of adding a duplicate.
  - **Delete** removes the shortcut and it stops working. You still need to remove the icon from your home screen yourself, because Android doesn't let apps do that. If you tap it later, it will say that the shortcut was deleted.

apps.description: Free, encrypted internet calls between friends, inside a complete replacement for your phone's Phone and Messages apps. Android, Kotlin, Jetpack Compose, Material 3; no ads, no tracking.
apps.releaseNotes:
## What's new

**ARK internet calls are now in the public release.** Create an ARK code in Settings, share it, link a friend's code on their contact card, and calls between you go over the internet — free, end-to-end encrypted (WebRTC with DTLS-SRTP), phone to phone. When the other phone cannot be reached the very same call goes over your carrier, so a call always goes through. An incoming ARK call rings on a locked, sleeping phone. Until you create a code the app makes no network connection at all; see the README for what the signaling server sees.

**Nine new languages:** Swedish, German, French, Spanish, Estonian, Russian, Portuguese, Italian and Polish, alongside English and Finnish. The app follows the device language; Android 13 and newer can pick a language per app.

**Backup to a file.** Settings → Backup saves your settings, blocking rules, speed dials, your ARK code with its linked contacts and the WhatsApp call history into one file, password-protected by default, and restores it on the same or another phone. Before anything is replaced, the restore shows which ARK code and how many linked contacts the file brings. Calls, messages and contacts are not included; they stay in Android's own backup.

**Do Not Disturb now treats an ARK call from a starred contact like a carrier call** from that contact: the incoming-call notification names the caller, so the "calls from contacts" exceptions match it.

The README has been rewritten and the step-by-step instructions moved to a [user guide](https://github.com/jrs8205/ARK-phone/blob/main/docs/USAGE.md).

Update from 1.27 in place; the APK carries the same signature and your data is kept. Requires Android 8.0 or newer.

apps.description: Android app store for open-source apps on GitHub. Developers publish an app by adding the topic "arkstore" to its repository; the store installs and updates APKs straight from GitHub releases.
apps.releaseNotes:
- **Several updates at once**: they go in order, three downloads at a time and the rest in a queue, the store's own update last; the next install prompt opens only once the system has settled the previous install. A download, waiting or running, is cancelled by tapping its ring, and an unasked update's download stops when the Wi-Fi is left, the charger unplugged or the switch turned off
- **Skip or hold back**: skip this version, or do not update this app at all, from the details of an update; the app moves to the installed ones with a note and is not counted, announced or installed unasked. The next version is offered again after a skip. Both go with the export
- **Screenshots and longer descriptions**: the details show the screenshots and the longer description a developer publishes in the repository's `fastlane/metadata/android/` folder, on GitHub, Codeberg or GitLab, in a source added on the device, or in the F-Droid and IzzyOnDroid catalogues; a screenshot opens to fill the screen
- **Automatic updates**: on Android 12 and later, a switch in the settings lets the background check install the updates of the apps the store itself installed without asking, only on Wi-Fi or only while charging if wanted
- **A GitHub token**, given in the settings, raises GitHub's limit of requests from 60 an hour for the whole network to 5,000; it goes to GitHub's API alone and stays out of backups, device transfers and exports
- **Export and import** of the sources, the bookmarks and the settings as a file, through the system's file picker
- **No source to begin with**: the store's own apps come from the index like everyone else's, so a fresh install asks GitHub for nothing. The accounts of the installed apps are asked directly about what was pushed since the index was built, so a new release of an installed app shows up at once
- **In 17 languages**: German, Spanish, French, Italian, Portuguese, Russian, Ukrainian, Polish, Dutch, Turkish, Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Arabic and Hindi join English and Finnish, in the app and in the store's own listing; the short description is shown in the device's language when the developer provides it
- The details tell when an installed app was last updated

Download `ARK-Store-1.8.0.apk` below and open it on your phone to install, or update from inside ARK-Store.

apps.description: Android device monitor with a home-screen widget, per-app usage insights and a charging screensaver. Fully offline - no internet permission. GPL-3.0-or-later.
apps.releaseNotes:
## What's changed

- **Optional extended access** through **Shizuku** (no root needed) or **root**, under Settings → Extended access. Off by default: nothing is read, no `su` is started and no Shizuku request is made until you switch it on, and the app still has no internet permission.
- With it on, the Home and Device tabs show the **real CPU load** instead of the frequency estimate, **chip temperatures** (CPU, graphics, surface), **graphics load**, and the **battery's health, cycle count, first-use and manufacturing dates** where the phone reports them.
- **Android's own battery statistics** on the since-charge page: drain per hour with the screen on and off, how long a full battery would last at that pace, each app's share, and what kept the phone awake (wake locks and wakeup reasons), explained in plain words (#3).
- Shizuku stops at every reboot: the switch stays on, says it is waiting, and the readings return by themselves once Shizuku is started again. Root that is revoked is given up after three refusals, and the switch says so.
- Phones without a battery charge counter show no drain pace rather than a false zero.

## Using Shizuku

Install [Shizuku](https://shizuku.rikka.app/), start it (wireless debugging on Android 11+, or ADB), then switch **Shizuku** on in Device Watch's Settings and allow the request. The readings are read-only; see PRIVACY.md for what the access covers.

## Installing

Updates cleanly over v1.4.x, v1.5.0 and v1.6.x. If you are coming from v1.3.1 or older (package `com.example.modernwidget`), uninstall the old app first — it is a different package and will not update.

Android-sovellus: Ilmatieteen laitoksen ja Open-Meteon sääennusteet rinnakkain, Suomen pörssisähkön hinnat ja FMI:n säävaroitukset. Nyt suomeksi, ruotsiksi ja englanniksi.

## Uutta versiossa 0.4.0

- **Kolme kieltä.** Sovellus seuraa puhelimen kieltä: suomi ja ruotsi omalla kielellään, kaikki muut kielet englanniksi. Kielen voi vaihtaa sovelluskohtaisesti Androidin asetuksista. Nimi on Sää & Sähkö, Väder & Börsel tai Weather & Spot Prices.
- Kellonajat, päivämäärät ja desimaalierotin seuraavat kieltä (esim. `12.10` ja `17.9.` suomeksi ja ruotsiksi, `12:10` ja `17 Sep` englanniksi).
- FMI:n varoitustekstit, varoitusilmoitukset ja Maanmittauslaitoksen paikannimet haetaan sovelluksen kielellä (esim. Borgå ruotsiksi). Jos varoituksen käännös puuttuu tai on vajaa, näytetään suomenkielinen teksti.
- Kielen vaihto päivittää näkyvän varoitusilmoituksen hiljaisesti, ilman uutta hälytystä.
- Tekstikoko seuraa puhelimen asetusta 150 %:iin asti; suuremmalla asetuksella sovellus käyttää 150 %:a, jotta näkymät pysyvät ehjinä. Alapalkin nimet mahtuvat kokonaan myös kapealla näytöllä.

## Asennus

- Vaatii Android 13:n tai uudemman (API 33). Kohdealusta Android 17 (API 37).
- Lataa `Saa-Sahko-0.4.0-release.apk` ja asenna. Päivitys aiemman version päälle säilyttää suosikit ja asetukset.
- Päivitettäessä 0.3.x:stä voimassa olevista säävaroituksista tulee kerran uusi ilmoitus, koska ilmoitusten tunniste muuttui.

- Paikkahaku vaatii oman Maanmittauslaitoksen API-avaimen käännösvaiheessa; julkaistussa APK:ssa se on mukana.
